note.label: 2 Chronicles 29: Hezekiah Cleanses the House of the Lord

precepts.why:
“And these are the singers, chief of the fathers of the Levites, who remaining in the chambers were free: for they were employed in that work day and night.” The singers among the Levites were employed in that work day and night. That is the ordained pattern of temple music, and Hezekiah restored it.

He “set the Levites in the house of the Lord with cymbals, with psalteries, and with harps, according to the commandment of David, and of Gad the king’s seer, and Nathan the prophet”. And “when the burnt offering began, the song of the Lord began also with the trumpets, and with the instruments ordained by David king of Israel. And all the congregation worshipped”, “until the burnt offering was finished.”

Then the king and the princes “commanded the Levites to sing praise unto the Lord with the words of David, and of Asaph the seer. And they sang praises with gladness, and they bowed their heads and worshipped.” The singers were back at the work they were set to.

note.label: Ezra 2: The Register of Those Who Returned

precepts.why:
“So all Israel were reckoned by genealogies; and, behold, they were written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah, who were carried away to Babylon for their transgression.” Israel kept its register: every man's father's house and seed was written down, and the book went with them into the captivity.

That is why those from Tel-melah, Tel-harsa, Cherub, Addan and Immer, who “could not shew their father’s house, and their seed, whether they were of Israel”, were set aside. And the children of the priests who “sought their register among those that were reckoned by genealogy” and were not found were “as polluted, put from the priesthood”, forbidden to eat of the most holy things “till there stood up a priest with Urim and with Thummim.” The genealogy was the proof of who was Israel, and without it a man could not stand in the priesthood.

points: All Israel were reckoned by genealogies and written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah, who were carried away to Babylon for their transgression.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 9: The Returned Inhabitants and Their Offices

points: The first inhabitants who dwelt again in their cities were the Israelites, the priests, Levites, and Nethinims, and in Jerusalem dwelt the children of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh, numbered by their genealogies.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 9: The Returned Inhabitants and Their Offices

points: The priests who returned are named, Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jachin, and Azariah the ruler of the house of the Most High, with the heads of their houses.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 9: The Returned Inhabitants and Their Offices

points: The Levites who returned are named, very able men for the work of the service of the house of the Most High.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 9: The Returned Inhabitants and Their Offices

points: The porters are named, Shallum the chief and his brethren, who waited in the king's gate eastward and kept the gates of the tabernacle as their fathers did before them.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 9: The Returned Inhabitants and Their Offices

points: David and Samuel the seer ordained them in their set office, and they had the oversight of the gates on the east, west, north, and south, lodging round about the house of the Most High because the charge was upon them.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 9: The Returned Inhabitants and Their Offices

points: Certain of them had charge of the ministering vessels, and others were appointed over the fine flour, wine, oil, frankincense, and spices, and some of the priests made the ointment of the spices.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 9: The Returned Inhabitants and Their Offices

points: Mattithiah had the set office over the things made in the pans, and the Kohathites prepared the shewbread every sabbath, showing all the offices these brethren held.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 9: The Returned Inhabitants and Their Offices

points: The singers, chief of the fathers of the Levites, remained in the chambers free from other work, for they were employed in the work day and night.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 9: The Returned Inhabitants and Their Offices

points: The chapter returns to Gibeon and repeats the line of Ner, Kish, and Saul, tracing Saul's sons and the house of Jonathan down through Micah to Azel.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 9: The Returned Inhabitants and Their Offices

points: Azel's six sons are named to close the record, joining this genealogy to the reign of Saul that follows.
